name: Laguna S 2.1
tagline: The West's open-weights answer, licensed under Linux Foundation paper
description: Poolside's 118B-total / 8B-active MoE coding model with a 1M-token context and switchable thinking modes — pre-trained in under nine weeks on 4,096 H200s. Ships in BF16 plus official FP8, INT4, and NVFP4 builds, an XS sibling, and community GGUFs; a free no-login demo runs at chat.poolside.ai.
why: 70.2% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 40.4% on DeepSWE puts it in the ring with models 10–20× its active size, and it's the rare Western frontier-lab release with weights you can pull today. The OpenMDW-1.1 license is the story: Linux Foundation-backed, MIT-grade in substance — and the same license we already had to make a judgment call on for Cosmos 3.
useCases: Self-hosted agentic coding backends with 1M-token context
Terminal and repo-scale automation on a single DGX-class box
Fine-tuning a competitive Western base for code domains
audience: Coding-agent builders; teams wanting non-PRC open weights

setup.requirements: Runs on a single NVIDIA DGX Spark; official INT4/NVFP4 and community GGUF builds bring it toward workstation reach

license.notes: Same call as Cosmos 3, same reasoning: OpenMDW-1.1 grants rights 'without restriction' across copyright, patent, database, and trade-secret law, with attribution-only conditions and a litigation-termination clause — no use restrictions, no output claims. Substantively as open as MIT. But it is not OSI-approved, and our bright line is OSI approval, so we downgrade rather than round up. Flagged for review.

tally.stars: Six official HF repos at launch (base, FP8, INT4, NVFP4, XS); unsloth GGUFs within days

limitations: Benchmarks concentrate on coding and terminal work rather than general chat, several hosts cap context below 1M, and independent evaluation of the launch numbers is still thin.
take: poolside spent years closed. Its first open drop uses the most open model license on the shelf — the only thing between it and 'open' is OSI's docket.
